name: FinDash
description: FinDash (findash.tech) is a free web app that turns a small business's monthly figures, from an Excel or CSV spreadsheet or a photo of a supplier invoice, into a profit and loss (P&L) dashboard of revenue, costs, profit and budget vs actual, with plain-language AI advice. It is not accounting software.
featureList: Reads Excel and CSV spreadsheets in any layout
Reads photos of supplier invoices and receipts (with a free account; more with Plus)
Monthly revenue, costs in four groups, gross profit, net profit and net margin
Net profit trend and a budget estimator
Advice written by AI (with a free account; more with Plus)
Export to Excel, print or save as PDF

mainEntity.name: Is there a free profit and loss dashboard for small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. FinDash is free, and the dashboard works without an account. Add a spreadsheet of your monthly totals to see each month's revenue, costs, gross and net profit, and how much of your budget you used.

mainEntity.name: Do I need QuickBooks or Xero to use FinDash?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Fill in FinDash's Excel or CSV template, or use your own layout: columns are matched by name, and a sheet with the months across the top is turned the right way round. If you use QuickBooks or Xero, copy each month's totals from your Profit and Loss report.

No. Your spreadsheet is read and added up in your own browser. Only the things you ask for that need a server leave your computer: reading an invoice photo, writing advice, or saving your figures to a free account. The privacy policy lists exactly what is sent.

mainEntity.name: Can FinDash read a photo of a supplier invoice or receipt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a free account, and more of them each month with FinDash Plus. Claude, an AI model, reads every line; FinDash checks the arithmetic against the printed total; and you confirm the lines before anything is added to your month.
Your total costs as a share of the spending budget you set for the month. Over 100% means you spent more than you planned, and the month shows up under What needs attention.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gross profit is revenue minus direct costs: cost of goods sold, labor, employee meals and payroll tax. Net profit is what is left after every cost, and net margin is net profit as a share of revenue.
No. It shows profit: each month's revenue minus its costs. Cash can differ, for example when customers pay late or you buy stock ahead, so a profitable month can still leave you short of cash.

mainEntity.name: Does it work for restaurants, shops and trades?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. FinDash was built for a restaurant, and its four cost groups work just as well for shops, trades, service businesses and freelancers. Figures can be in dollars, euros, pounds and other currencies.
No. It doesn't connect to your bank, keep your books, send invoices, take payments, run payroll or file taxes. It shows the figures you already have, clearly, so you can act on them.

Prime cost is your cost of goods sold (food and drink) plus your total labor: wages, payroll tax and staff meals. It is usually the largest part of a restaurant's spending. FinDash shows it each month as the direct costs group, as a share of sales.

mainEntity.name: What is a good prime cost for a restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Full-service restaurants often aim for about 60 to 65% of sales, and quick-service a little lower. Much above that leaves little room for rent and everything else. How your own prime cost moves from month to month matters more than any one target.

mainEntity.name: What is a good food cost percentage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Food cost is commonly quoted at about 25 to 35% of sales, depending on the menu and the concept. FinDash shows it each month as cost of goods sold divided by sales.

mainEntity.name: What is a good net profit margin for a restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restaurant margins are thin: full-service restaurants often keep around 3 to 5% of sales as net profit, and a slow month can easily turn into a loss when rent and other fixed costs stay the same.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the numbers from my POS or accounting software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Copy each month's totals from your Profit and Loss report in QuickBooks or Xero, or from your POS sales reports, into FinDash's template. FinDash doesn't connect to your POS or accounting software; it reads the spreadsheet you give it.

mainEntity.name: Does FinDash replace my bookkeeper or accountant?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. FinDash doesn't keep your books, run payroll or file taxes. It turns the monthly totals you already have into a clear picture of food cost, labor, prime cost and profit, so you can see where the month went.
